summaries.title: Core slugify: lowercase, hyphen separators, input validation
summaries.search_text: core slugify: lowercase, hyphen separators, input validation # task-001: core slugify ## goal deliver the smallest useful `slugify(text)`: lowercase, every run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes one hyphen, no leading/trailing hyphen, and a `typeerror` for non-strings. non-goal for this task: accented letters (task-002) and length limits (task-003). ## acceptance trace | acceptance | scenario | test | result | |---|---|---|---| | ac-001 | sc-001 | `ac-001 turns words and punctuation into a lowercase hyphenated slug` | pass | | ac-002 | sc-002 | `ac-002 collapses separator runs and trims leading/trailing hyphens` | pass | | ac-003 | sc-003 | `ac-003 rejects non-string input with a typeerror` | pass | | ac-004 | edge case | `ac-004 returns an empty string when nothing slug-worthy remains` | pass | ## tdd evidence recorded by `hepha record-check` in `.hepha/evidence/task-001.json`. | phase | command | exit | meaning | |---|---|---:|---| | red | `node --test test/slugify.test.js` | 1 | 4/4 tests fail against a `not implemented` stub | | green | `node --test test/slugify.test.js` | 1 | first attempt ran before the implementation was saved; gate kept the task in `doing` | | regression | `npm test --silent` | 1 | same cause as above | | green | `node --test test/slugify.test.js` | 0 | 4/4 pass with the minimal implementation | | regression | `npm test --silent` | 0 | full example suite passes | ## what changed - `src/slugify.js`: type guard, `tolowercase()`, `/[^a-z0-9]+/g → "-"`, trim hyphens. - `test/slugify.test.js`: one test per acceptance criterion, named by ac id. - `package.json`: `npm test` runs the suite with the built-in runner. ## reviews - spec review (claude-spec-reviewer): passed — each ac maps to exactly one test. - code review (claude-code-reviewer): passed — notes that accented letters are currently treated as separators (`crème` → `cr-me`); that is task-002's scope. - human approval: recorded after this summary. - browser check: not applicable (library, no ui). ## asset candidate - policy: `candidate` - candidate: `.hepha/wiki/candidates/chk-001.md` — edge cases worth testing for any slug function. ## risks and follow-ups - non-ascii letters are dropped entirely until task-002 lands.

summaries.title: Fold accented Latin letters to ASCII
summaries.search_text: fold accented latin letters to ascii # task-002: fold accented latin letters to ascii ## goal `crème brûlée à la carte` must become `creme-brulee-a-la-carte` instead of `cr-me-br-l-e-la-carte`. non-goal: transliterating non-latin scripts or locale rules such as `ß` → `ss`. ## research four options compared in `decision-log.md` (dec-001). chosen: `normalize("nfkd")` + strip `\p{m}`. a probe showed nfd would miss ligatures and full-width letters, and that `ø`, `ß`, `ł` are not decomposable — accepted as a documented limitation. ## acceptance trace | acceptance | scenario | test | result | |---|---|---|---| | ac-005 | sc-004 | `ac-005 folds accented latin letters to their ascii base letter` | pass | | ac-006 | non-goal guard | `ac-006 does not transliterate non-latin scripts` | pass | ## tdd evidence | phase | command | exit | meaning | |---|---|---:|---| | red | `node --test test/slugify.test.js` | 1 | ac-005 failed (`cr-me-br-l-e-...`); ac-006 already passed — it guards existing behaviour | | green | `node --test test/slugify.test.js` | 0 | 6/6 pass | | regression | `npm test --silent` | 0 | 6/6 pass, task-001 behaviour unchanged | ## what changed - `src/slugify.js`: two lines — `normalize("nfkd")` and `replace(/\p{m}+/gu, "")` before lowercasing. - `test/slugify.test.js`: ac-005, ac-006. - `.hepha/decision-log.md`: dec-001. ## reviews - spec review: passed. code review: passed (see evidence notes). human approval recorded after this summary. ## asset - policy: `required` → published `pat-001` "strip diacritics with nfkd + \p{m}". ## risks and follow-ups - scandinavian/german/polish users get partially folded slugs (`søren` → `s-ren`). revisit only with a concrete need.

assets.title: Strip diacritics in JavaScript with NFKD + \p{M}
assets.search_text: strip diacritics in javascript with nfkd + \p{m} pattern unicode slug javascript normalization # strip diacritics in javascript with nfkd + \p{m} ## conclusion to fold accented latin letters to ascii without a dependency: ```js text.normalize("nfkd").replace(/\p{m}+/gu, "") ``` prefer **nfkd** over nfd: it additionally folds compatibility characters (`fi` → `fi`, full-width `abc` → `abc`). ## when it applies - slugs, search keys, file names, sort keys for latin-script text. - any node.js ≥ 10 / modern browser (`\p{...}` needs the `u` flag). ## when it does not - letters that are not "base letter + combining mark" survive unchanged: `ø`, `ß`, `ł`, `æ`, `đ`. handle them with an explicit table only if users need it. - non-latin scripts are not transliterated (`你好` stays `你好`). - do not use it to display names — it is lossy. ## how to verify ```text "crème brûlée" -> "creme brulee" "final abc" -> "final abc" "søren" -> "søren" (unchanged, known limitation) ``` ## source task-002 under spec-001/sc-004. the test `ac-005` failed before the change and passed after it; options compared in dec-001.

assets.title: Edge cases to test for any slug function
assets.search_text: edge cases to test for any slug function checklist slug testing strings # edge cases to test for any slug function ## conclusion a slug function looks trivial, but most bugs live in the same five places. write one test per item before writing the regex. ## checklist - [ ] punctuation between words (`hello, world!` → `hello-world`). - [ ] runs of mixed separators (`a -- _ b`) collapse to a single hyphen. - [ ] leading and trailing separators are trimmed — no `-hello-`. - [ ] input that contains nothing slug-worthy (`!!!`, `""`) returns `""`, not `-`. - [ ] non-string input throws instead of slugifying `"null"` or `"42"`. ## when it applies - any ascii slug for urls, file names, anchors or ids. ## when it does not - slugs that must preserve non-latin scripts — the checklist is still useful, but the expected outputs differ. ## source derived from task-001; every item corresponds to an assertion in `test/slugify.test.js` that was seen failing before it passed.
